_comment: BUG-76 — the shared contract between the server's reading of a note body and the editor's.
Since 43-H2 the body is the ONLY source of the agenda, so a line the server counts and the
header does not show is a topic the user can neither see nor tick, while the 'X / Y' pill goes
on counting it.
Both sides assert this file, so neither reading can drift alone:
server — tests/Domain.Specs/Projections/AgendaParityFixtureSpec.cs (AgendaFromContent.Parse)
client — web/src/__tests__/agendaParity.test.ts (agendaEditorApi.readTopics)
Fields per case:
markdown     the stored note body, exactly as both sides receive it
topics       what the SERVER reads: text + ticked state, in document order
header       what the HEADER reads, present ONLY where it differs from `topics`
divergence   why they differ and why it is not closed here; required whenever `header` is
present, so a real gap can never be hidden by quietly adding an override
The register covers bodies the EDITOR can produce. Two divergences are deliberately left OUT
of it — this is not a claim that no others exist, only that these two are excluded and why.
Both are PRE-EXISTING — neither is reached by widening the topic walk to nested
lists — only imported or hand-written markdown gets to them, and the first save normalises
both away. Verified against a real editor, and ASSERTED rather than left as prose — see
agendaParity.test.ts, 'the divergences left out of the register really are normalised by a
save'. A tiptap-markdown upgrade that stopped hoisting, or a serializer that stopped fencing,
turns those tests red instead of turning this paragraph silently false.
`1. [ ] Numbered task` — the server's marker class is [-*+], so it reads no topic. The
client reads one, but NOT through the numbered list: the parser leaves the orderedList
item empty and hoists a sibling TOP-LEVEL taskList, which the walk has always read.
Saving rewrites the line as `- [ ] Numbered task` and the two agree again. The save is
NOT lossless: it also leaves a stray empty `1. ` item in the note. That item is inert —
neither side reads it as a topic — but it is visible, so do not call the save clean.
a 4-space-indented code block holding a checklist line — the server counts it (its only
code rule is a ``` / ~~~ fence), the client sees a codeBlock and reads none. Saving
re-emits it fenced, after which the server skips it too.

cases.name: a checklist nested under another task item
a checklist nested under a plain bullet
a checklist nested under a numbered item
a checklist two levels down, under a bullet under a task item
cases.markdown:
- [ ] Budget (Q3)
  - Cloud spend
    - [ ] Storage tier
- [ ] Hiring plan

cases.name: an item with no text yet
a blockquoted checklist is someone else's agenda
a checklist inside a fenced code block is code
inline emphasis is not part of the topic text
escaped brackets read as the characters the note shows
a checklist line holding only an image (KNOWN DIVERGENCE, open)
cases.divergence: The editor's markdown parser cannot put an image inside a checklist line: a note image is a BLOCK node, so the parser hoists it out of the task item and leaves the item genuinely empty (`taskList > taskItem > paragraph(empty)`, then a sibling `image`). Nothing in the item is skipped, because nothing is there — so no change to the topic walk can close this. Closing it means making note images inline in the editor schema, which must also fix the same shape's destructive round-trip: re-serialising this body yields `- [ ] \n\n![Burn-up chart](notes/n1/burnup.png)- [ ] Hiring plan`, which glues the next checklist line onto the image and loses it as a topic on the next save.

cases.name: a checklist line holding an image and text (KNOWN DIVERGENCE, open)
cases.divergence: Same block-image hoist as the image-only case, and the same reason it cannot be closed in the topic walk — but the text is hoisted out too, into a sibling paragraph, so the topic loses its words as well as its checkbox. Its round-trip is not destructive, so it is the milder half of the pair. This is the shape NoteEditor.test.tsx drives, because it is the one whose reading CHANGES between the mount-time (image-stripped) document and the resolved one.

cases.name: a topic containing a link (KNOWN DIVERGENCE, open)
cases.divergence: The header shows the link's TEXT, the server shows the link's markdown. Both are readings of the same line and neither is wrong on its own: the editor holds a link mark over the words, so textContent is what the note displays, while the server reads the raw line and CHANGE-38's StripInlineMarks strips emphasis but not link syntax. Count, order and ticked state agree — only the label differs — so nothing is miscounted and no command addresses the wrong line. Registered rather than left out because, unlike the two divergences in the header comment above, this one SURVIVES the round-trip: no save normalises it, so it is permanent until the server's strip learns link syntax (the fix belongs there, in AgendaFromContent, not in the walk — the header is already showing what the user sees).

cases.name: a topic containing an emoji shortcode (KNOWN DIVERGENCE, open)
cases.divergence: The header shows the emoji, the server shows the shortcode that produced it. The app loads note content through `emojifyMarkdown`, so `:rocket:` is already unicode before the parser sees it, while the server reads the stored line as written. Count, order and ticked state agree — only the label differs. SELF-HEALING, unlike the link and image cases: the editor now holds the unicode character, so the next save writes `- [ ] Ship it 🚀` and the two agree from then on. Asserted rather than described — see agendaParity.test.ts, 'the divergences left out of the register really are normalised by a save'. Registered anyway, because until that save happens it is a live divergence on real content, and the register is the contract.
